title.zh: 癌症放射免疫治疗制造联合体
title.en: Manufacturing consortium for cancer radioimmunotherapy

aliases: Manufacturing consortium for cancer radioimmunotherapy

registry_record.name: Manufacturing consortium for cancer radioimmunotherapy
registry_record.objective_original: GlyTherix is an Australian SME developing antibody treatments for cancer. Radioimmunotherapy (RIT) uses antibodies to selectively deliver radiation to kill cancer cells, while limiting damage to healthy cells. Despite its tremendous potential, widespread adoption of RIT has been limited by the complex manufacturing process and short shelf life of the radioisotope. This project brings together Australian SMEs, Universities and Government research organisations CSIRO and ANSTO to pioneer manufacturing of “shake-and-bake” kits that allow on-site, on-demand production of RITs in hospital radiopharmacies. Miltuximab antibody will be used as a testbed for the entire production process and testing safety and efficacy in a Phase 1 clinical trial.
partners: Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation

Radioimmunotherapy (RIT) uses antibodies to selectively deliver radiation to kill cancer cells, while limiting damage to healthy cells. Despite its tremendous potential, widespread adoption of RIT has been limited by the complex manufacturing process and short shelf life of the radioisotope. This project brings together Australian SMEs, Universities and Government research organisations CSIRO and ANSTO to pioneer manufacturing of “shake-and-bake” kits that allow on-site, on-demand production of RITs in hospital radiopharmacies. Miltuximab antibody will be used as a testbed for the entire production process and testing safety and efficacy in a Phase 1 clinical trial.

title.zh: 黄铁矿制电池级钴与硫
title.en: Novel processing of pyrite ore to produce battery grade cobalt and sulfur ***

aliases: Novel processing of pyrite ore to produce battery grade cobalt and sulfur ***

evidence.locator: Novel processing of pyrite ore to produce battery grade cobalt and sulfur ***

registry_record.name: Novel processing of pyrite ore to produce battery grade cobalt and sulfur ***
registry_record.objective_original: The Project will assess and optimise Cobalt Blue's (COB) innovative metallurgical process for efficiently treating previously uneconomic pyrite-cobalt ore to produce battery precursor cobalt sulfate and elemental sulfur. A demonstration plant will operate continuously on up to 1000t of concentrate over 12 months to simulate full scale production. Operational parameters, material properties, process controls and mass/energy fluxes will be measured, modelled and optimised, and product analysis will be undertaken on the calcine and sulfur to ensure product specifications are met. If proven, it is expected the new metallurgical process will enable a doubling of Australia's cobalt production from previously uneconomic pyritic feedstocks.
partners: Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation

summary.en: The Project will assess and optimise Cobalt Blue's (COB) innovative metallurgical process for efficiently treating previously uneconomic pyrite-cobalt ore to produce battery precursor cobalt sulfate and elemental sulfur. A demonstration plant will operate continuously on up to 1000t of concentrate over 12 months to simulate full scale production. Operational parameters, material properties, process controls and mass/energy fluxes will be measured, modelled and optimised, and product analysis will be undertaken on the calcine and sulfur to ensure product specifications are met. If proven, it is expected the new metallurgical process will enable a doubling of Australia's cobalt production from previously uneconomic pyritic feedstocks.

registry_record.objective_original: With the increasing electricity prices, Australian households and business have continued to embrace PV solar panels. In 2018, six PV panels were installed per minute on average. The increase of popularity is likely to result in end-of-life issues in terms of disposal of waste, with a total of 1.5 M tonnes of waste modules estimated by 2050 in Australia. A process will be developed to fully recover glass from PV panels. The CRC-P will provide essential support to the applicant and partners to commercialise recycled glass from PV solar panels.

registry_record.name: Wireless mining conveyor technology to Improve safety and reduce outages
registry_record.objective_original: MineSensor combines proprietary hardware, firmware, software, and an analytics platform to digitise mine conveyor information to reduce breakdown, increase mine output and improve safety. A fitted transponder measures conveyor roller bearing temperature and roller thickness. Information from the transponder is received and analysed, resulting in reports and alerts. MineSensor and the University of Newcastle developed the IP, patented the technology, created a prototype, and undertaken laboratory performance testing at the University of Newcastle. With Reliable Conveyor Belt we are conducting field trials at a Hunter Valley coal mine. This project will take the MineSensor field prototype to a mid-scale trial, then to pre-commercial release.

title.en: Enhanced Influenza Vaccine Production: New vaccine manufacture substrates

aliases: Enhanced Influenza Vaccine Production: New vaccine manufacture substrates

evidence.locator: Enhanced Influenza Vaccine Production: New vaccine manufacture substrates

registry_record.name: Enhanced Influenza Vaccine Production: New vaccine manufacture substrates
registry_record.objective_original: Influenza (flu) is a global health issue, causing severe illness and deaths each year. Flu vaccines, key to flu prevention, are produced in eggs, a process that suffers considerable production hurdles, using almost 1.6 billion fertilised chicken eggs per year and producing tonnes of flu infected waste. To solve this major industry problem, we have developed new vaccine production substrates (eggs and cell lines) that can produce significantly higher quantities of flu vaccine, alleviating the production hurdles of this vital medical product. This project will take our highly developed prototypes and deliver a translated, commercially viable products for international sale. Our eggs and cell lines will save time, money and lives.

title.zh: 可持续高纯氧化铝生产
title.en: Sustainable High Purity Alumina Production

aliases: Sustainable High Purity Alumina Production

registry_record.name: Sustainable High Purity Alumina Production
registry_record.objective_original: Impact Minerals has developed a High Purity Alumina (HPA) production process which addresses both the environmental and operational cost challenges of standard methods. Leveraging expertise from Edith Cowan University, the project integrates Membrane Selective Technologies to the process to increase the purity of HPA to <50ppm contaminants and recycle wastewater and acid by removing impurities, enabling a ‘Zero Liquid Discharge’ closed loop process. CPC Engineering will design and construct a Pilot Plant for process demonstration and optimisation. By demonstrating the use of membrane technologies for separating iron, aluminium and other metals, the project is potentially transformational across Australia’s critical minerals industry.

registry_record.name: Commercial scaling of microplastic removal from industrial wastewater
registry_record.objective_original: This project aims to build on the successful NSW Small Business Innovation & Research 2021 Water Purification Challenge prototype by scaling and validating a microplastics wastewater purification technology in a real-world setting. It will enhance commercial readiness for market launch. No viable solution currently exists for removing microplastics in the 1–100 µm range. The patented technology will remove microplastics and fine suspended solids from industrial laundry wastewater using chemical coagulation and ultra-high-speed centrifugation. The solution features real-time sensors and AI-driven digital twin optimisation for precise control. Modular, scalable, and cost-effective, improving compliance, efficiency, and sustainability while enhancing industry competitiveness.

registry_record.objective_original: Mining operations need to embrace novel technologies to overcome the challenging dilemma of increased demand for critical minerals whilst committing to sustainability. All partners will benefit from the established collaboration under the CRC-P framework and expand their capabilities for emerging mining methods.

title.en: Transforming Nickel Ore Processing with Low-Cost Low-Emission Molten Sulfur

aliases: Transforming Nickel Ore Processing with Low-Cost Low-Emission Molten Sulfur

evidence.locator: Transforming Nickel Ore Processing with Low-Cost Low-Emission Molten Sulfur

registry_record.name: Transforming Nickel Ore Processing with Low-Cost Low-Emission Molten Sulfur
registry_record.objective_original: This project aims to develop a low-cost and low-emission alternative to High-Pressure Acid Leaching (HPAL) for nickel laterites. Laterites hold >65% of global nickel resources yet only ~15% of Australia’s nickel production comes from them due HPAL’s high costs, environmental harm, and sulfuric acid reliance. Oxleigh Recycling Technologies and partners are leading a $7.8 million effort to adapt, scale, and validate a molten sulfur technology originally developed for battery recycling for nickel laterite processing. A pilot plant will demonstrate more than 50% cost, 85% water, and 90% emission reductions, defining commercial adoption pathways. The project could reverse Australia’s nickel mine closures, declining refined output, and falling export earnings.

registry_record.objective_original: This project aims to advance onshoring pectin production through advanced, energy-assisted manufacturing, reducing environmental waste, and generating circular economy benefits. Pectin, found in fruits (especially citrus and apple), is used as a gelling, thickening and stabilising agent in food products like jams and yogurts. It is valued for its natural, plant-based and flavour enhancing properties. In many applications there is no substitute available making pectin an essential ingredient. Converting fruit waste into pectin and fibre is a zero-waste operation. Feedback from pectin users has confirmed strong support for an all Australian made, reliable, high-quality pectin.

aliases: Developing a Scalable Green Plasma-Based Perchlorate Manufacturing Process

evidence.locator: Developing a Scalable Green Plasma-Based Perchlorate Manufacturing Process

registry_record.name: Developing a Scalable Green Plasma-Based Perchlorate Manufacturing Process
registry_record.objective_original: Ammonium perchlorate is required for manufacture of energetic materials for defence, a national priority area, as well as for space access, mining and battery manufacturing. The concept of producing perchlorates using a plasma-based process is highly innovative and is a technological step change. Plasma synthesis of perchlorates is an alternative to traditional electro-chemical methods, with benefits in increased purity, output and energy efficiency. This project aims to develop a cost effective, modular system that is scalable and will produce perchlorates using this environment-friendly, waste-free production technology. This will provide the feedstock required to manufacture ammonium perchlorate for DefendTex’s solid rocket motors.

registry_record.name: Hot loads: Advancing fire tech for lithium battery fires in waste trucks
registry_record.objective_original: Improper disposal of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) causes over 12,000 fires annually across Australia’s refuse trucks and processing facilities. IKON services will collaborate with RMIT University and industry partners to develop an advanced multi-sensor detection suite capable of early identification and intervention for LIB-related fires in waste trucks. The project will deliver a field-validated, sensor platform that integrates multiple sensing modalities, coupled with an oxygen-dilution response mechanism designed to suppress secondary fuel combustion before it escalates. The project will also explore complementary waste collection systems to enhance the resilience of Australia’s waste management infrastructure.

registry_record.objective_original: Ferronova is a SME developing super-paramagnetic iron-oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs) for image guided cancer surgery and therapy. This vision aligns with Siemens, a global leader in cancer imaging and radiotherapy. Nanotechnology has been widely researched in oncology, but clinical translation has been limited by complex manufacturing and limited effectiveness in vivo. The CRC-P will address these issues to develop commercial scale manufacturing of Ferronova’s FerroTrace SPION platform, with the testbed being FerroTrace-FAPi, a preclinically validated theranostic product for image guided radiotherapy and proton therapy. The safety and effectiveness of FerroTrace-FAPi will be evaluated in a Phase 1b clinical trial in glioblastoma.

aliases: Regenerable Carbon for Eliminating Forever Chemicals in Water

evidence.locator: Regenerable Carbon for Eliminating Forever Chemicals in Water

registry_record.name: Regenerable Carbon for Eliminating Forever Chemicals in Water
registry_record.objective_original: This project will focus on the removal of per- and poly-fluroalkyl substance (PFAS) in water treatment that relies on carbon-based adsorbers. These absorbers have limited surface functionality that reduces efficiency, especially for short-chain PFASs. End-of-life sorbents are also classified as hazardous waste, posing disposal risks due to potential leaching. The project aims to develop functionalised ceramified carbon-based adsorbers with high PFAS adsorption properties, adaptable to various pressures and flow rates and capable of multiple reuse cycles. Thermal regeneration of the materials will convert the adsorbed PFAS into benign chemicals. Thus, this project will support sustainable water treatment, enhance sovereign capability, and deliver environmental/social benefits for Australia.

registry_record.objective_original: This project will develop, validate and scale an organic solvent-free hydrometallurgical process to recover>95% high-purity metals from lithium-ion battery waste. Led by Green Li-ion with the partners, it will advance from bench-scale (TRL 4) to fully automated pilot-scale (TRL 7), making a closed-loop system for battery materials. Through this process, recyclers can produce battery-grade nickel, cobalt and manganese (in lower operational and capital cost), strengthening Australia’s sovereign capability. Shifting from spent batteries sales to high-value salts boosts profitability nearly fourfold, while automation of the pilot unit enhances efficiency, safety, and sustainability, positioning Australia as a leader in clean energy technologies.

registry_record.name: Carbon to Commodity- The CO2 Circular Economy
registry_record.objective_original: Australia faces the dual challenges of cutting carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions and reducing reliance on imported soda ash, a product essential for glass, detergent, and chemical production. This project will pilot a portable carbon capture and utilisation (CCU) system that simultaneously captures fermentation-derived CO2 and converts into soda ash product with >99.9% purity. Led by Net Zero Stack and collaborating with RMIT, UCLM (Spain) and local industry partners within the supply chain, the project will fabricate a decentralised CCU process, conduct trials at wineries, and validate soda ash products with end-users. The approach significantly lowers CO2 emissions, builds sovereign capability, and positions Australia to advance its 2050 net zero goal.
partners: Barossa Grape and Wine Association Incorporated

registry_record.objective_original: Exosomes are small particles released by cells. They are the key effector in cell therapies and have the potential to be an off-the-shelf medicine without the technical problems of cell therapies. Currently exosomes are made at small scale - this project aims to develop a large-scale advanced manufacturing process for exosomes. This project will focus on exosomes to treat peripheral vascular disease (a limb-threatening condition often associated with diabetes), with other diseases to follow.

title.en: Integrated platform for removing forever chemicals from water and solids

aliases: Integrated platform for removing forever chemicals from water and solids

evidence.locator: Integrated platform for removing forever chemicals from water and solids

registry_record.name: Integrated platform for removing forever chemicals from water and solids
registry_record.objective_original: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are increasingly detected in Australia’s wastewater treatment plants, contaminating effluent, accumulating in biosolids, and posing long-term environmental and health risks. Existing remediation methods often struggle with complete PFAS removal from both water and solids and often require substantial capital investment for plant upgrades. This project aims to integrate and operate the patented magnetic sorbent at pilot and full-scale within the existing plants, efficiently removing PFAS to undetectable levels without altering current operations. The treated water and biosolids can be safely discharged and reused, protecting Australia’s environment and communities, including regional populations.

registry_record.objective_original: This project seeks to pioneer an innovative technology that converts organic waste into high purity biomethane, organic fertiliser, and clean water, with zero waste. registry_record.name: A scalable conversion system to upcycle hard-to-recycle wastes to graphene
registry_record.objective_original: EQ Plastics, partnered with RMIT and Rapid Auto, pioneers a ground-breaking initiative aimed at developing a semi-automated conversion system to convert kg-scaled hard-to-recycle plastics and tyre waste into graphene in minutes. Through developing an upscaled rapid arc-discharge pyrolysis system, the project promises a swift and environmentally friendly approach to waste conversion. registry_record.objective_original: The Project will scale-up patented bio-polymer technology to enable the recycling of comingled and contaminated waste plastics, without the need to sort the waste stream. The process overcomes the problem of how to achieve a circular economy in waste plastics, by using a series of organic polymers in its process to separate atomic bonds in the plastic so it can be reconstituted to the desired formulation, without any loss in strength or other properties. The process converts contaminants into inert non-toxic molecules. The process will maximise opportunities for waste plastic to be recycled into valuable new products throughout the domestic and international supply chain, without the need to retrofit existing manufacturing equipment.

registry_record.name: Modular ammonia manufacturing via a breakthrough carbon-free process
registry_record.objective_original: Decarbonisation of ammonia production is a global priority. The current process contributes approx. 1.8% of global CO2 emissions, even as it remains an essential component of global food security via fertiliser production. The Jupiter Ionics team has developed unique, world-leading technology for the electrochemical production of green ammonia. This project will bring together a consortium to conduct R&D to address scale-up and manufacturing challenges associated with developing prototypes capable of producing 0.5 t/year and beyond, which will underpin the rollout of the first commercial versions of the device. This initial scale of device will be targeted towards localised manufacture of fertilisers in various sectors of agriculture.

registry_record.objective_original: This automation project will integrate Edge AI with advanced sensors to focus on reducing costly defects during die-casting of aluminium EV parts. Robotic spectral imaging sensors will detect microscopic defects with support from Edge AI processing of multi-modal sensor data. Concurrently, Edge AI methods running locally will optimise production automation through root-cause analysis. Lead partner APTA Automation will provide Australian firms with Edge AI solutions in advanced automated manufacturing to increase global competitiveness, upskill the Australian workforce, and achieve enhanced sustainability.

registry_record.objective_original: This CRC-P will introduce smart analytical platform based on AI to optimise material recovery at Dasma’s materials recycling facility (MRF). Data from this platform can be shared. Using this data, MRFs, recyclers and manufacturers can plan the supply chain to increase the use of recovered resources. This CRC-P will also develop a prototype smart manufacturing plant to develop new building products. The aim is to manufacture products that can compete with the current market to eliminate negative value stream of the recovered raw material by market diversification. This end-to-end manufacturing is a solution to add value and efficiency by having visibility across the supply chain. This how CRC-P funding will pave the way towards application of industry 4.0 principles in waste management.

registry_record.name: SiPHyR: A new technology for affordable net-zero hydrogen production
registry_record.objective_original: This project will demonstrate the feasibility of a breakthrough lower-carbon hydrogen production technology “SiPHyR”, featuring a patent-pending reactor that uses stored renewable heat. It decomposes methane via pyrolysis yielding hydrogen and solid carbon, but no CO2 emissions. SiPHyR is scalable, with strong potential to produce net-zero hydrogen continuously for ~US$1/kg. The project will de-risk and accelerate SiPHyR’s commercialisation with a prototype demonstration and by addressing challenges in methane pyrolysis, to enable Australia’s transition to lower-carbon hydrogen.

title.en: Upscaling a Novel Technology for Recycling Lithium-Ion Batteries

aliases: Upscaling a Novel Technology for Recycling Lithium-Ion Batteries

evidence.locator: Upscaling a Novel Technology for Recycling Lithium-Ion Batteries

registry_record.name: Upscaling a Novel Technology for Recycling Lithium-Ion Batteries
registry_record.objective_original: The Project is developing a novel process for recycling lithium-ion batteries. The technology processes the ‘black mass’ from waste batteries into precursor material that can be re-used to manufacture new lithium-ion batteries. Project partners - Oxleigh, the University of NSW, Scimita Operations, Envirostream Australia and Worley - are undertaking an $8.1 million collaborative venture to advance the development and commercialisation of the process. The Project will fully develop and upscale a safe and environmentally sustainable process that can treat up to 5.5 tonnes/year of black mass from NMC-type lithium-ion batteries to recover at least 80% of the lithium, nickel, manganese, and cobalt metals as salts at greater than 90% purity.

registry_record.name: Revolutionary upcycling of landfill waste into hydrogen, fuels & materials.
registry_record.objective_original: Bioelektra has developed a novel municipal solid waste (MSW) process producing 70% recyclables and 30% biomass (the latter currently for landfill). No commercial technology exists to upcycle this biomass resource into valuable products. This CRC-P aims to transform waste biomass into hydrogen (H2) fuel and char/inorganic ash for potential exploitation by Cement Australia & the Ash Development Association of Australia in construction. A bio-refinery demonstration unit, employing additive manufacturing for catalyst fabrication, underpins the proposed process. Technoeconomic analysis will identify the potential for H2 use in future Bioelektra MSW collection trucks and/or export.

aliases: Healing Australian Carbon Wounds Using Hemp Plantation and Construction

registry_record.name: Healing Australian Carbon Wounds Using Hemp Plantation and Construction
registry_record.objective_original: Industrial hemp plant sequesters 8-15 ton of CO2-e per hectare, twice as effective as forests. This project proposes to use hemp farming as a solution to offset carbon emissions by the Australian industry; and use the hemp plant as innovative timber alternative. Australia is facing a shortage in timber supply due to increased housing demand and bush fires and push to halt deforestation by 2030. This CRC-P aims to develop sustainable alternatives to timber products using well-established manufacturing technologies and innovative advanced processes. The proposed end-to-end approach will add value and efficiency by having visibility across the supply chain, leading to offsetting Australian industry's CO2 emissions and net-zero requirements.

registry_record.objective_original: The Halion Loop is cheaper, cleaner and significantly more versatile than existing technology for the production of copper and other critical metals. An Australian invention, it is designed to create strategic and value-added domestic supply chains. This project will advance the most novel aspects of the technology from TRL 4 to 6. Multidisciplinary science and engineering teams, operating at the Macquarie University Deep Tech Incubator, will conduct bench and pilot stage research. registry_record.objective_original: Conventional processing of copper-nickel-platinum group metals (Cu-Ni-PGM) deposits extracts the metals by flotation with the resultant concentrate sent offshore for smelting. aliases: Smart AI-enabled automation and upcycling solution for plastic recycling.

evidence.locator: Smart AI-enabled automation and upcycling solution for plastic recycling.

registry_record.name: Smart AI-enabled automation and upcycling solution for plastic recycling.
registry_record.objective_original: Since many foreign countries restrict import of waste, the Australian government is implementing a ban on the export of waste from 2021 and an 80% resource recovery rate by 2030. However, the generation of substantial amount of no-value plastic residue in recycling plants results in unprofitable landfill cost while reducing the overall plant efficiency and profitability. This CRC-P will develop and commercialise an AI-enabled autonomous sorting system and automated plant and polymer technology needed to upcycle residue plastics. The proposed sorting system and value-added products will increase Australia’s recycle capacity by 42,000 tonnes per year and divert 16,800 tonnes per year of plastic residue from landfill and foster a circular economy.

aliases: Increased recycling of plastics by sensing and treating label contamination **

evidence.locator: Increased recycling of plastics by sensing and treating label contamination **

registry_record.name: Increased recycling of plastics by sensing and treating label contamination **
registry_record.objective_original: This project focuses on increased re-use of HDPE plastic. Recycling companies today have problems in recycling HDPE because labels contaminate the mix. HDPE is a high quality material in demand for re-use but under 20% of used HDPE is now recycled. Increasing re-use represents tens of millions of dollars to industry. A partnership of technology, recycling and manufacturing companies will work with university experts in sensors, polymers, systems engineering and environmental policy to overcome this problem. CRC-P support will be used to identify a novel way to sense and treat residual contaminants on chips of HDPE in the recycling process. This will be unique worldwide and designed for industrial use for a broad range of plastics.

registry_record.objective_original: This project seeks to solve the biggest problem affecting cancer patients having surgery; the risk of cancer cells being left behind after an attempted curative operation. title.zh: 快速非接触式太阳能电池检测
title.en: Next-Generation Solar Inspection: Fast, Contactless, and Australian-Made

aliases: Next-Generation Solar Inspection: Fast, Contactless, and Australian-Made

evidence.locator: Next-Generation Solar Inspection: Fast, Contactless, and Australian-Made

registry_record.name: Next-Generation Solar Inspection: Fast, Contactless, and Australian-Made
registry_record.objective_original: Traditional current-voltage (I-V) testers are not suitable for next-generation solar cells. They cannot reliably make electrical contact, they damage cells, their throughput is limited to 7,000 cells/hour, and they cannot detect issues at early fabrication stages. This project aims to commercialise automated, contactless I-V systems that eliminate physical probing, prevent damage, double throughput, enable early-stage screening, and offer performance mapping instead of only an average value. Globally, the project aims to replace 600 of >2,000 old testers and install 1,200 new systems. A market share >$200M is projected with trained personnel capable of supporting the doubling of BTi's workforce anticipated by the project end.

title.en: Holistic Economical Offshore Wind Turbine Solution for Australia

aliases: Holistic Economical Offshore Wind Turbine Solution for Australia

evidence.locator: Holistic Economical Offshore Wind Turbine Solution for Australia

registry_record.name: Holistic Economical Offshore Wind Turbine Solution for Australia
registry_record.objective_original: Offshore wind is globally recognised for its potential to provide clean, affordable energy while also contributing to economic growth, but Australia lags in implementing it due to technological complexities, regulatory frameworks, and ecological impacts. Typically, installing wind turbine offshore involves steps using heavy machinery, leading to extended assembly time and increased costs compared to onshore installation. aliases: Green hydrogen energy production and storage for distributed energy systems

evidence.locator: Green hydrogen energy production and storage for distributed energy systems

registry_record.name: Green hydrogen energy production and storage for distributed energy systems
registry_record.objective_original: Endua is unique in hydrogen technology because it solves green energy for small-scale, decentralised power systems. The Endua green hydrogen power bank will produce and store energy on-demand for regional Australia, replacing diesel generators. Ampol’s 40% diesel market-share provides a direct sales channel to this $1.5b market across agriculture, mining, telecommunications and communities. Australia’s transition to renewables will falter if we cannot solve the long duration energy storage problem. The CRC-P will support Endua to develop a green energy storage solution sooner, reducing costs by 90% and emissions by 203Mt. This will trigger mass adoption of green energy storage that will catalyse the uptake of renewables.

title.en: Green microfactories for recycling waste plastics into engineered products **

aliases: Green microfactories for recycling waste plastics into engineered products **

evidence.locator: Green microfactories for recycling waste plastics into engineered products **

registry_record.name: Green microfactories for recycling waste plastics into engineered products **
registry_record.objective_original: Single use plastics are a significant national problem, currently stockpiled at Australian landfills and waste management sites. The project plans to turn this enormous challenge into an opportunity to create high quality engineered product for manufacturers via distributed microfactories. The project develops an advanced, semi-automated manufacturing technology by which waste plastics are efficiently transformed into high value products at smaller scales than previously feasible, enabling recycling microfactories to be implemented locally. The process is modular, scalable and closed loop with zero waste. The product will be used to manufacture unique street furniture and linked to manufacturers nationwide.

title.en: Recycled plastic ROBOVOID construction solution. **

aliases: Recycled plastic ROBOVOID construction solution. **

registry_record.name: Recycled plastic ROBOVOID construction solution. **
registry_record.objective_original: ROBOVOID is a revolutionary recycled plastic construction solution to enable the recycling of up to 6 million tonnes of plastic per year around the world. The solution involves clever modular recycled plastic parts that displace concrete that is not necessary to achieve the performance requirements of structures. The engineered voids result in weight savings of up to 75% and widespread adoption will result in a global CO2 emission reduction of up to 3%. CRC-P support will enable the project team to conduct the necessary testing and development to achieve a reliable and economical solution that can be exported to the global market.
partners: The Trustee for GT Recycling Unit Trust
